narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Machinist's Bench"**

tinkerbench is a workbench, not a dashboard. Surfaces are aluminium and graphite, cool and matte, with nothing on them that is not a tool or a reading. Coolant blue carries code keywords and focus. Marking yellow is the scribe's paint: it appears only as small marks (the logo, the active tab, the dark-theme editor cursor). Every feed card carries a colored left edge like a coded tool handle, so its kind reads before its label does.

The system is precise and restrained. It is flat, ruled by thin lines, and dense enough to hold a full run's worth of queries, logs, and dumps beside an editor for hours. Hover is a faint tint, never a lift. The one moving moment is the timeline bars drawing out along their scale, like a reading being taken.

It rejects the stock GitHub look it replaced: no Primer palette, no GitHub editor themes, no tiny all-caps labels.
keyCharacteristics: Two themes, light (aluminium) and dark (graphite), driven by the same CSS custom properties.
Flat, line-ruled layout; depth only for overlays.
IBM Plex Sans for prose and controls, IBM Plex Mono for code, keys, and numbers.
Kind colors on card edges; danger and warning override kind.
Yellow is a mark, never a fill.

rules.name: The Marking Paint Rule
rules.body: Yellow is only ever a small mark: the logo, the active tab, the cursor. It is never a fill, a button, or a background.

rules.name: The Coded Handle Rule
rules.body: A feed card's left edge (3px) names its kind: Query blue, Log green, HTTP violet, View steel. Danger and warning replace the kind color, because a broken or slow entry matters more than what kind it is. Kinds without a color keep a Scribe Line edge.

rules.name: The Full-Strength Text Rule
rules.body: Text never uses an opacity-reduced token (`text-muted/70`) and code never sits on Aluminium Canvas in a color that only passes on Bench Surface. Every text pair holds 4.5:1 in both themes; check the light theme first, it is the tighter one. Decorative marks hidden from assistive technology (the breadcrumb slash) and disabled controls are the only exceptions.

rules.name: The Quiet Brackets Rule
rules.body: Bracket pairs in the editor stay ink-colored. Colored nesting levels would compete with the kind colors.

rules.name: The Machine Voice Rule
rules.body: Monospace is for code, keys, and numbers. UI prose, labels, and error messages are always sans.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: No all-caps labels and nothing below 12px. Acronyms keep their case ("N+1", "HTTP", "SQL").

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Numbers that sit in a column or update in place (tab counts, run summary, timeline, line buttons) use tabular figures so they don't jitter. Card footer durations are plain caption text today; give them tabular figures if they ever line up across cards.

rules.name: The Flat Bench Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the bench casts a shadow. A shadow means "this is floating above your work and will go away."

dos: **Do** add every new color as a CSS custom property with a light and a dark value, and check both themes.
**Do** give a new feed kind its own edge color only if it is signal; otherwise leave it on Scribe Line.
**Do** use the global Coolant Blue focus ring; replace it only with an equally visible Coolant Blue border.
**Do** keep the Monaco theme hexes in step with the CSS tokens; Monaco cannot read custom properties.
**Do** keep numbers tabular and in Plex Mono.
**Do** collapse long content behind an explicit Show all / Show less control instead of clipping it with CSS.
donts: **Don't** use the stock GitHub/Primer palette or GitHub editor themes.
**Don't** use yellow for anything but small marks (logo, active tab, cursor).
**Don't** use all-caps micro labels or any text below 12px.
**Don't** color bracket pairs or add syntax colors that compete with the kind colors.
**Don't** add shadows to anything that sits on the bench; shadows are for overlays only.
**Don't** add motion beyond state feedback; the timeline draw-in is the one moving moment.
